what: What did each Lunenburg town employee earn in 1965?
why: `report-gross-wages` holds per-employee earnings from the 1995-2010 reports and FY2011-FY2025. The 1965 annual town report prints no wage list: the whole text (138 pages) was searched for payroll, gross, wage and salary and found only aggregates (`Total Payroll $933,594.85` and `Number of Persons on Payroll 359`, p12; payroll deductions, p25 and p29), the accountant's lines (p31-43) and the school personnel listing (p118-128), which names staff, subject, grade, years and year appointed and prints no pay (sources/data/report-tables/1965/). — closes: the Town's calendar-1965 payroll register (W-2 totals by employee) from the Treasurer's office.

what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in 1965?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1965 report records the new Article 15 by-law on a personnel classification and compensation plan (p74-80, effective March 8, 1965) and one expense, `Wage Classification and Compensation Plan` (p21, p29), and not the schedule; searched classification, salary schedule, grade and step across the whole text; `salary schedule` appears nowhere (sources/data/report-tables/1965/). — closes: the Personnel Board's Classification and Compensation Plan as adopted at the March 6, 1965 Annual Town Meeting.

what: What did each special revenue fund take in, spend and carry forward in 1965, town-wide?
why: `special-revenue-funds` holds forward, receipts, disbursements and balance by fund from the 1995-2010 reports. The 1965 report prints year-end balances of the lunch, athletic and adult-education programs as appropriation balances on the balance sheet (p21: School Lunch Program 2,870.64; School Athletic Program 226.99; Adult Education Self-Supporting 51.00), the lunch program's own report (p134) and the School Department's special accounts (p112-115); no town-wide receipts-and-disbursements schedule by fund. Searched revolving and special revenue: `revolving` appears only for a street sweeper on p72 (sources/data/report-tables/1965/). — closes: the Town Accountant's calendar-1965 special revenue fund ledger.

what: What was appropriated, spent and carried forward on each capital project in 1965?
why: `report-capital-projects` holds a capital project fund schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1965 report prints each project as an article in the accountant's schedule (p31-43) and as a balance-sheet appropriation balance (p21), and the Planning Board describes a `Capital Budget Program` in prose (p60) without printing one; searched capital across the whole text (sources/data/report-tables/1965/). — closes: the Planning Board's capital budget program, if one was prepared, or the Town Accountant's 1965 capital projects ledger.

what: What was Lunenburg's assessed valuation by property class, its levy, overlay and new growth for 1965?
why: `report-valuation` holds valuation and levy history from the 1987-2010 reports. The 1965 report prints the total assessed valuation, the real estate and personal property parts of it, and the tax rate in the `About the Town` list (p4: $11,810,645 = $10,983,935 + $826,710; $89.00) and by year 1950-1965 (p8, landed), and the overlay as balance-sheet lines (p20-21: `Overlay Deficit - 1964 levy` 726.52; `Overlay Reserved for Abatements (1965)` 6,141.82); no valuation by class beyond those two, no levy, no new growth. Searched valuation, overlay, recapitulation and new growth: the one `recapitulation` hit (p66) is in the Nashoba health district's prose (sources/data/report-tables/1965/). — closes: the Board of Assessors' 1965 tax rate recapitulation.

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1965, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fee schedule from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1965 report gives the count in prose (p56: `Of the 158 weighing devices inspected in 1965, 136 were found to be correct and sealed, 20 were adjusted and sealed and 2 condemned`), the Sealer's fees as a receipt (p25 `Sealer's Fees 177.30`) and an expense (p27 `Sealer of Weights and Measures 559.20`); no table of devices by type and no fee schedule. Searched sealer and weights and measures: p27, 34, 56, 76, 136 (sources/data/report-tables/1965/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1965 annual report to the Town.
